name: 6x6 mm tactile push button
//: One of the remote's five controls. Two terminals, no polarity, no part number worth having — a 6x6 through-hole tactile switch is a commodity and the only variable that matters is cap height.

needs.note: To a GPIO. The other terminal goes to a rail, and WHICH rail decides the polarity — see host_requirements, because on this family of chips it also decides whether the board can wake from sleep at all.

power.note: Pressed pulls the GPIO to ground, so the pin idles HIGH on a pull-up and reads 0 when pressed. THIS IS A DESIGN DECISION WITH A CONSEQUENCE: see host_requirements.

//pin_order: A 6x6 tactile switch has four legs in two pairs, and each pair is one terminal — so a 2-pin footprint is the electrical truth and a 4-pad footprint is the mechanical one. `pushbutton` in footprinter gives four pads wired as two nets, which is what a board wants; this record describes the two terminals.

body_mm.source: the 6x6 form factor's defining dimension; the variable is CAP HEIGHT, not footprint
body_mm.note: Height is 4.3, 5, 8 or 12 mm depending on variant and is the only thing to check against an enclosure.

host_requirements: Decide the polarity against deep sleep, not convenience. On an ESP32 every armed ext1 wake pin shares ONE trigger level, so a board with two wake sources must have them assert in the same direction. A button to ground asserts LOW and forces WAKEUP_ALL_LOW, which is an AND across the whole mask — with two sources armed, the board wakes only when both assert at once. If this button is a wake source, wire it to 3V3 behind a pull-down instead and arm WAKEUP_ANY_HIGH.

Give it an external pull, not just the internal one. Internal pulls are inactive for the ~300 ms between reset and firmware and through any reflash, which for a wake input means a floating pin while the chip is asleep.
Debounce in firmware, not hardware, unless the button is also a wake source — a wake pin's first edge is the one that matters and it is not debounced by anything.

debounce_ms_typical.source: the conventional figure for a tactile dome switch; not measured on any specific part
debounce_ms_typical.why_it_matters: too short double-fires a control, too long makes a remote feel broken. On a driving remote it is the difference between steering and twitching.

cap_height_mm.source: a variant, not a fact about the family
cap_height_mm.why_it_matters: the only dimension that decides whether the enclosure closes

wokwi.stand_in: Wokwi's pushbutton: either side of a pair is the same contact; no bounce is modelled
